input.strategy_title: Adopt structured JSON logging across RHOAI components
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RHOAI components log in inconsistent formats — plain text, key=value, and
ad-hoc JSON — which breaks centralized log queries and makes support cases
expensive: correlating one user request across Dashboard, serving, and
pipelines requires per-component parsing rules. The platform needs one
structured logging convention, and each component needs to adopt it. Component
adoptions are independent of each other once the convention exists.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema, required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id), and library guidance per language (Go, Python, TypeScript). |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | KServe controller and serving runtimes emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Data Science Pipelines (operator and API server) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | Model Registry emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | TrustyAI services emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Notebooks (notebook-controller) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Training Operator emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Documentation describes the log format and example queries for common support scenarios. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry
- TrustyAI
- Notebooks
- Training Operator

## Out of Scope

- Log storage, retention, or forwarding infrastructure
- Metrics and tracing conventions (logging only)

## Open Questions

None — the convention work (HLR-1) is prerequisite design, and per-component
adoptions are mechanical once it lands.

# Publish platform structured JSON logging convention

## Description

This epic delivers the platform-wide structured logging convention that all
RHOAI components will adopt: a JSON schema for log records, the set of
required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id), and
library guidance for each of the platform's implementation languages (Go,
Python, TypeScript). This is the prerequisite design work for every
per-component adoption; component adoptions are mechanical once it lands.
The convention is a platform design artifact owned by the RHOAI Observability
function; the destination repo for the published convention is not named by
the strategy and must be confirmed with the owning team before work starts.

## Scope

- Define and publish the JSON log-record schema, including the required
  fields: timestamp, level, component, namespace, and correlation id.
- Publish library guidance per language for producing convention-conformant
  logs: Go, Python, and TypeScript.
- Socialize the convention with the adopting component teams (Dashboard,
  serving, pipelines, model registry, TrustyAI, notebooks, training operator)
  and collect their acknowledgement before the document is considered final.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The logging convention document is published and versioned in its
  destination repo.
- The JSON schema fully specifies the required fields (timestamp, level,
  component, namespace, correlation id) and their formats.
- Library guidance exists for Go, Python, and TypeScript.
- All adopting component teams have reviewed and acknowledged the convention
  (recorded sign-off).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema,
  required fields, and library guidance per language.

# Adopt structured JSON logging in Dashboard

## Description

Convert the Dashboard's log output to the platform structured JSON logging
convention so that its records can be queried and correlated centrally without
component-specific parsing rules. The Dashboard is the web console through
which user requests originate, so its logs carry the correlation ids that
downstream components' records are joined on.

## Scope

- Replace the Dashboard's current logging (plain text / key=value / ad-hoc
  JSON) with output conforming to the published platform logging convention.
- Ensure every emitted record carries the required fields: timestamp, level,
  component, namespace, and correlation id, using the TypeScript library
  guidance from the convention.
- Propagate the correlation id across the request boundaries the Dashboard
  handles so a single user request can be traced from the console into serving
  and pipelines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All Dashboard log output parses as JSON records conforming to the published
  convention schema, with all required fields present.
- A user-initiated action in the Dashboard produces log records carrying the
  same correlation id across the request path.
- The existing Dashboard build pipeline remains green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs.
